acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Skeletons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Rattler, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Scatter-and-Reform Initiate (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A loose, gap-toothed humanlike frame that appears ready to fall apart, with dull socket pinpoints, a rusted shortsword, incomplete hands, and no binding armor.

Signature mechanic: Loose Muster: a strong interruption scatters the Rattler into a skull, ribcage, and limb piles; dull socket pinpoints travel down visible rune scratches and pull the nearest pieces back unless the skull is displaced or struck before the ribs stand.
battlefieldDuty: Probe target selection with brittle shortsword pressure, then turn one strong hit into a short reassembly puzzle centered on the loose skull.
constructionDimensions: Bone and grave goods become a drowned-sepulcher system: waterlogged ivory, algae-dark mail, shell-inlaid runes, fluid-filled marrow channels, wet grave-cloth, and pressure valves built into shields or staffs.

Surface and motion show coherent flow through wet reflections, visibly filling bones, narrow jets from joint holes, trailing cloth runoff, draining socket channels, and pressure loss that changes articulation.
counterplay: Scatter it away from other bone piles, then kick or strike the skull before the ribcage rises; destroying ordinary limb fragments alone only delays the same reassembly. Affinity signal: A marrow channel fills toward one joint and a shell valve lifts before movement; opening that valve drains the binding fluid and leaves the connected bones loose.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only water treatment without waterlogged materials, marrow flow, and pressure articulation
Glow-only water treatment without coherent channels, valves, or drainage
Shapeless water fill that removes skeletal negative space
Opaque mist or spray that conceals bones, seals, or pressure valves
identityInvariants: Human or humanoid skeletal proportions remain narrow, angular, and defined by empty negative space where flesh and organs would be.
Bone white or yellowed ivory is paired with rust, black iron, tattered grave-cloth, and one explained necromantic socket-fire accent such as green, blue, or gold.
Bone, rusted mail, corroded steel, grave-cloth, funerary jewelry, and crowns remain recognizable mortuary materials rather than living anatomy.
Carved skull runes, bone spurs, fused armor-like mass, grave regalia, and orbiting fragments accumulate as binding power becomes denser.
Bone density and the intensity and reach of the visible necromantic binding escalate together, but every form preserves gaps, joints, or binding anchors that can be deliberately broken.
telegraph: Gap teeth chatter, the frame visibly loosens at every joint, and the dull socket pinpoints draw thin lines toward the nearest dropped bones.
